Meeting header: 2025-06-11 16:00 PDT | Duration: ~62m | Attendees: Alex Morgan (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Diego Ramos (DS), Jordan Lee (Summit Head of Search), Anita Gupta (ML Eng), Victor Salazar (Product), Samantha Kim (Security)

Summary (auto): demo of hosted embeddings + reranker pipeline, integration patterns, benchmark plan, security Qs, next steps.

[00:00] Alex Morgan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — Alex from Redwood here, I'll kick us off, um, quick agenda: API demo, Console walkthrough, and then optimize/cost suggestions.
[00:14] Jordan Lee: Great, thanks. We're mostly focused on improving product search relevance and ranking for the storefront. Right now we're using Elastic for text search and a small vector layer for semantic matches.
[00:26] Priya Patel: Nice, can you say a little about your traffic profile and latency targets? That helps shape recommendations.
[00:33] Jordan Lee: Sure, p95 latency budget is 150ms for the search endpoint. Peak QPS is about 120 QPS on holiday, normally 20-30 QPS. Average doc size — product descriptions + specs — about 1.2k tokens after normalization.
[00:49] Anita Gupta: We also have a business constraint: results must be deterministic for A/B experiments and TTLs are short, we can't keep long-term user PII with third parties.
[00:59] Alex Morgan: Totally, we can talk SSO + data retention in the Security section; Redwood Hosted API can be used without storing raw payloads if you want — there's an option to disable logs and use customer-managed KMS for keys.
[01:12] Victor Salazar: Primary ask is: can we boost recall for ambiguous queries and then rerank to respect business rules?
[01:18] Priya Patel: Yes — typical two-stage pipeline: 1) recall via embeddings (approx nearest neighbors) or hybrid recall (Elastic + vector) 2) rerank via Redwood's reranker endpoint that takes both the original query and top-K candidates and returns scores. We'll demo both flows.
[01:32] Alex Morgan: I'll share my screen — Console -> Hosted API -> Models. So here is the embeddings endpoint example call, simplest curl, returns a vector for each doc or query.
[01:45] [screen demo noise - typing]
[01:58] Priya Patel: Important tip — choose embedding model based on dimensionality and downstream reranker. Lower-dim embeddings are faster in vector DB but might lose fine-grained semantics; Redwood Optimize will recommend a profile based on your eval set.
[02:12] Jordan Lee: How do we store these vectors? Do you force us to use a hosted vector DB?
[02:17] Diego Ramos: You don't have to. People use Pinecone, Weaviate, or even Elastic with vector plugin. Redwood's hosted API just returns embeddings; we also have a managed vector store option for Dedicated customers, but for hosted most customers manage vectors in their DB and call our reranker.
[02:34] Anita Gupta: Ok and what's the latency if we do recall from a remote vector DB + call reranker? Concerned about double network hops.
[02:41] Priya Patel: Good question — typical pattern: recall top 50 locally (vector DB) then call reranker which only scores those 50 candidates. The reranker call itself is usually low latency — in hosted mode p50 p95 varies by model, but we can configure smaller reranker models for low latency. Latency might add ~30-80ms depending on model and sequence length. We'll run benchmarks for you.
[03:01] Jordan Lee: That might push p95 beyond 150ms on peak though.
[03:06] Priya Patel: That's where caching and batching come in — Redwood Console has prefix/KV cache that caches reranker results for repeated queries, and dynamic batching can improve throughput without impacting p95 for single-shot interactive queries. Also consider a smaller reranker for production and larger reranker for periodic re-ranking in background.
[03:23] Victor Salazar: Can you show the reranker API payload?
[03:28] Alex Morgan: Sure — here's an example: POST /v1/rerank with query, candidates array, and optional metadata like business_rules. It returns scores and a sorted list. We'll demo a live example with Summit sample.
[03:43] [typing, run demo call]
[03:55] Anita Gupta: I see some underscores in the transcript — I think the transcriber messed up 'KV cache' as 'K-V cash' earlier.
[04:01] Priya Patel: Yeah, transcription aside, here's the live output — reranker moved product B above product A because it matched the query intent better and respected a promotion tag.
[04:14] Jordan Lee: Does the reranker allow hard business rules (e.g., always keep sponsored items in top 3)?
[04:20] Priya Patel: You can pass business_rules as structured metadata to the reranker; we support post-score constraints too in the Console routing layer to enforce business constraints. The trick is to keep the rerank model aware but still deterministic for experiments.
[04:36] Victor Salazar: How about overall costs — for 120QPS peak, roughly how many tokens are we charged for?
[04:42] Alex Morgan: Cost depends on embedding model and reranker model tokenization. Broadly, for query+50 candidates rerank you may see X tokens per request — we'll put a spreadsheet with estimated token counts in the follow-up. Redwood Optimize can suggest batching and quantization to reduce token processing and GPU time.
[05:01] Jordan Lee: Are there customers who run both recall and rerank purely in Redwood?
[05:05] Priya Patel: Hosted flows typically run recall in your vector DB and rerank with us; Dedicated customers sometimes move vector store onto the same VPC so both recall+rerank are low-latency. We can discuss Dedicated if you need co-located storage.
[05:18] Samantha Kim: On security: are logs stored? How do we ensure PII is not persisted in hosted?
[05:24] Alex Morgan: By default we retain request metadata for troubleshooting but you can opt out: redact input, disable logs, or set retention windows. For enterprises we offer Private deployment and can configure KMS/HSM and audit logging. We'll send SOC2 + privacy docs.
[05:40] Samantha Kim: And SSO?
[05:43] Priya Patel: SAML/SSO supported via Console admin; RBAC for routes and models.
[05:48] Anita Gupta: One technical deep dive question: how does the reranker handle long candidate contexts? Our product pages are long.
[05:55] Priya Patel: Reranker uses truncation strategies: chunking candidates and providing summarized context, or use long-context reranker models if you want full page. Redwood Optimize can recommend model and chunk size tradeoffs for accuracy/latency.
[06:12] Jordan Lee: Can you show the Console routing page?
[06:15] [screen] Alex Morgan: Here — per-route settings, model pinned, autoscaling policy, batching window, and cache TTL. You can set a route to use hybrid recall by tagging it to call an external vector DB first.
[06:29] Victor Salazar: We saw weird ranking regressions after a model update last time — how do you guard against that?
[06:36] Priya Patel: We recommend canary rollouts and using Redwood's evals tied to prompt sets — you can pin a model version to a route, run A/B, and Redwood will compare eval metrics before full rollout. You can also set automatic fallback to previous model if quality drops.
[06:50] Jordan Lee: Awesome. Ok, demo looked good. Let's talk pilot plan.
[06:53] Alex Morgan: Proposed pilot: Redwood hosted API pilot for 4 weeks — we ingest your 10k doc snapshot into your vector DB (customer-managed), Redwood SE runs benchmark on recall+rerank with your queries. We measure recall/ndcg and latency; deliver a recommendation pack (model choices + Console config).
[07:08] Anita Gupta: What's the cost of the pilot?
[07:11] Alex Morgan: Pilot is free for evaluation — we just ask for dataset and engineer time. If you move to Dedicated later we'd discuss reserved capacity pricing.
[07:20] Jordan Lee: Sounds good.
[07:22] [the rest of the call is Q&A and minor clarifications, timestamps every ~30-90s to follow]
[07:30] Victor Salazar: A couple practical items: how do we version embeddings when product descriptions change frequently?
[07:37] Diego Ramos: You can do incremental embeddings for changed docs and keep an embedding version in metadata. For experiments we recommend snapshotting an eval dataset. Redwood Console can track model/embedding version in route metadata.
[07:48] Jordan Lee: Any gotchas with Elastic as vector store?
[07:52] Priya Patel: Elastic works; watch out for nearest-neighbor recall performance at scale. Also some Elastic variants use approximate search that affects recall. For better latency we often recommend an optimized vector DB or co-located Dedicated options.
[08:06] Anita Gupta: For the reranker scoring: what format are scores returned in? Are they calibrated probabilities?
[08:11] Priya Patel: We return normalized scores and can map to probabilities; you can also request raw logits for offline calibration. The Console will display distribution histograms for score analysis.
[08:23] Jordan Lee: Ok, final security question — does Redwood sign BAAs?
[08:27] Alex Morgan: For enterprise we do support BAAs in contracts; we'll route this to legal and solutions.
[08:34] Samantha Kim: Please send any SOC2 + compliance docs.
[08:36] Alex Morgan: Will do.
[08:39] Jordan Lee: Alright, let's confirm next steps.
[08:42] Alex Morgan: Recap: Alex will send API quickstart + pricing + Console screenshots; Priya will run the 1k-query benchmark once Summit shares sample data; Summit to provide 10k snapshot and queries; schedule pilot kickoff.
[08:56] Jordan Lee: Thanks everyone, that was helpful.
[09:00] Alex Morgan: Thanks! We'll follow up with an email and calendar invite for the pilot kickoff.
